overview: This one-page file inventory lists three State Department papers concerning an Indigenous Taiwanese uprising under Japanese colonial rule. The reports, sent from Japan and Taihoku between October 31 and December 9 of an unspecified year, describe the destruction of villages, deaths among Japanese and Formosans, uncertainty and speculation about the causes, and later observations on the event, apparently identified in the OCR as the “Mus. & Affair.”

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning racial disturbances in Taiwan
subfiles.about: An administrative inventory summarizes three reports concerning an uprising in Japanese-ruled Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists reports no. 36 from Japan by Forbes, no. 53 from Taihoku by Young, and no. 58 from Taihoku by Reed. The first reports an uprising that destroyed several villages and killed substantial numbers of Japanese and Formosans while speculating about its causes. The second says that no definite cause could yet be established, and the third records observations on what the inventory calls an uprising of “Savages” in Taiwan, apparently connected with the “Mus. & Affair.”

interest: The sheet is useful as a concise archival roadmap to three reports made at different stages of a colonial uprising: an immediate account, a follow-up emphasizing uncertainty about its causes, and a later set of observations. It also preserves revealing contemporary language, including “Formosans” and the colonial label “Savages,” and suggests that the reports concerned the event abbreviated by the OCR as the “Mus. & Affair.” Because the underlying reports are not present in the supplied text, the inventory is also evidence of their former placement and basic contents.
